nodes.label: Unused create-next-app Asset Set
nodes.rationale: All five public SVGs are untouched create-next-app scaffolding. The as-built shell uses Lucide React for icons and never references them, so they are dead weight in the bundle's public dir.

nodes.label: Unmodified create-next-app README
nodes.rationale: Still the generated boilerplate: it points at app/page.tsx, but the app was relocated to src/app/page.tsx - stale relative to the as-built layout.

nodes.label: File/Document Glyph Icon
nodes.rationale: A 16x16 monochrome outline of a page with a folded corner and text lines - a generic document marker.

nodes.label: Globe Glyph Icon
nodes.rationale: A 16x16 monochrome globe with latitude/longitude arcs - the conventional 'web / external link' marker.

nodes.label: Next.js Wordmark
nodes.rationale: The Next.js logotype rendered as vector letterforms on a 394x80 canvas, filled #000 - unusable on this app's zinc-950 dark shell without an inversion.

nodes.label: Vercel Triangle Logo
nodes.rationale: A single white filled triangle on a 1155x1000 canvas - the Vercel mark.

nodes.label: Browser Window Glyph Icon
nodes.rationale: A 16x16 outline of a browser chrome window with three title-bar dots.

nodes.label: addWorkspace Resolves null Instead of Throwing
nodes.norm_label: addworkspace resolves null instead of throwing
nodes.rationale: A 409 on a duplicate name is an expected outcome of normal user input, so it becomes rendered error state rather than an unhandled promise rejection at the click handler.

nodes.label: ApiError status 0 for Unreachable Backend
nodes.rationale: status === 0 is reserved for requests that never reached the server (transport failure or CORS rejection), letting the UI distinguish 'backend said no' from 'backend unreachable'.

nodes.label: cn() Class-Composition Primitive
nodes.rationale: clsx (conditional joining) composed with tailwind-merge (last-write-wins conflict resolution), so a later w-16 correctly overrides an earlier w-64 instead of both being emitted. The single primitive for every conditional/collapsed-state style.

nodes.label: Fixed Dark-Mode-Default Shell
nodes.rationale: zinc-950/zinc-100 applied directly with no prefers-color-scheme branching and no light theme - one palette, no dual-theme surface area.

nodes.label: Fail-Fast Multi-File Upload
nodes.rationale: One invalid file rejects the entire batch: a request either fully succeeds or is rejected outright, never partially ingested - so the corpus can never end up in a half-written state.

nodes.label: Hand-Mirrored TypeScript Contracts
nodes.rationale: TS interfaces are hand-mirrored from the Python source of truth because no OpenAPI/codegen pipeline exists yet - which makes every drift between the two a manual-maintenance risk.

nodes.label: useWorkspaces() Throws Outside Its Provider
nodes.rationale: A missing wrapper fails loudly at the call site instead of silently yielding null state.

nodes.label: Filename Path-Traversal Hardening
nodes.rationale: Filename validation runs BEFORE any extension check or parsing, rejecting directory components and any '..' substring (catching Windows-style '..\' that Path.name would not strip on POSIX). Always a strict HTTP 400 - never silent sanitization - so a traversal attempt is a hard failure, not a degraded success.

nodes.label: Read Response Body Once as Text, Then Parse
nodes.norm_label: read response body once as text, then parse
nodes.rationale: Calling response.json() directly on a non-JSON error payload (an HTML 404 page, a proxy 502) throws an opaque parse error that masks the real status. extractDetail() then normalizes both FastAPI shapes: {detail: str} and Pydantic 422's {detail: [{msg}]}.

nodes.label: src/ Folder Convention Relocation
nodes.rationale: src/app is silently ignored whenever a root-level app/ also exists, so the CLI-generated app/ was relocated and the @/* alias repointed at ./src/*.

nodes.label: Stale Active-Workspace Selection Cleared on Refetch
nodes.norm_label: stale active-workspace selection cleared on refetch
nodes.rationale: fetchWorkspaces clears activeWorkspace when it is absent from the refreshed list, so a selection cannot outlive a server-side deletion.

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules (read node_modules docs first)
nodes.norm_label: next.js agent rules (read node_modules docs first)
nodes.rationale: Warns that this Next.js version has breaking changes versus model training data, so the shipped guides under node_modules/next/dist/docs/ are authoritative over recall.

nodes.label: Homograph Attack in venv bin (mitigated)
nodes.rationale: A localized homograph ('pithon' spelled with a Greek pi) was detected inside the virtual environment's bin directory and mitigated on Day 1 - a supply-chain-shaped incident found in the dev environment itself, not in application code.

nodes.label: Outstanding: window.prompt Placeholder for New Workspace
nodes.norm_label: outstanding: window.prompt placeholder for new workspace
nodes.rationale: Workspace creation uses window.prompt rather than an in-app form - a deliberate placeholder deferred out of Module 5.

nodes.label: Rule: No Hardcoded Secrets
nodes.rationale: API keys, DB credentials, and JWT secrets always load from .env - never literals in source.

nodes.label: Deterministic Network-Free Mock Fallback
nodes.rationale: Every external-AI service has a keyless mock path: embeddings are SHA-256-seeded numpy vectors (identical text always yields an identical vector), generation yields the top chunk word-by-word. No network, no model download, so dev and CI are fully offline and reproducible.

nodes.label: EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS as a Fixed Constant
nodes.rationale: 1536 is centralized in config.py but deliberately NOT a .env-configurable Settings field: changing it requires a schema migration, not a config edit.

nodes.label: localhost and 127.0.0.1 Are Distinct Origins
nodes.rationale: The browser must reach the app at http://localhost:3000, not http://127.0.0.1:3000: cors_allowed_origins defaults to the former only and the two are different origins to the CORS check.

nodes.label: Strict CORS Allow-List
nodes.rationale: Explicit origin allow-list from .env with allow_credentials=True, methods and headers narrowed to exactly what the API needs. No wildcard origins, methods, or headers - a wildcard is incompatible with credentialed requests anyway.

nodes.label: 58-Test Suite Across Modules 1-4
nodes.rationale: Each module closed at a 100% pass rate: 16 after Module 1, 22 after Module 2, 48 after Module 3, 58 after Module 4.

nodes.label: Route Registered at "" to Avoid a 307
nodes.norm_label: route registered at "" to avoid a 307
nodes.rationale: With the router's /api/v1/workspaces prefix, registering at "/" resolves to a trailing-slash URL and makes FastAPI 307-redirect the un-slashed URL the frontend actually calls - an extra hop that also interacts badly with the strict CORS allow-list.

nodes.label: Outstanding: No Committed Tests for GET /workspaces
nodes.norm_label: outstanding: no committed tests for get /workspaces
nodes.rationale: The Module 5 GET route was verified ad-hoc against in-memory SQLite fixtures; committed regression tests are still outstanding - the only route in the API without them.

nodes.label: Exact Chunk Offset Traceability
nodes.rationale: start_offset/end_offset are recomputed by forward-scanning text.find() rather than trusted from the splitter, so any chunk can be traced back to its exact source location - the substrate the whole verification story depends on.

nodes.label: Chunk-Size Drift: 800/150 logged vs 1000/200 as-built
nodes.rationale: WORKLOG Day 1 records the chunker as '800 token chunks, 150 overlap' while DESIGN.md documents the as-built default as 1000/200 characters. The two documents disagree on both the numbers and the unit (tokens vs characters); DESIGN.md is the as-built record. Flagged rather than silently reconciled.

nodes.label: Dialect-Portable Vector Column
nodes.rationale: A TypeDecorator whose impl is Text but whose comparator_factory is pgvector's Vector.Comparator: real VECTOR(1536) on Postgres, JSON-encoded Text elsewhere. Lets the ACTUAL production ORM models run against in-memory SQLite with no parallel test schema, while .cosine_distance() stays callable for query construction on every dialect.

nodes.label: Sentence-Level Claim Decomposition
nodes.rationale: An answer is split into sentence-level claims and each is scored independently, so verification is per-claim rather than per-answer and a single unsupported sentence is visible instead of averaged away.

nodes.label: No Local Model Downloads
nodes.rationale: No torch/transformers anywhere: claim verification uses a dependency-free keyword-coverage heuristic designed to be swapped for a real DeBERTa/cross-encoder later WITHOUT touching decomposition or aggregation logic.

nodes.label: Mandatory Regex Word-Boundary Matching
nodes.rationale: Every keyword-to-chunk match wraps the escaped keyword in \b on BOTH sides. Without it the claim keyword 'cat' would count as supported by source text containing 'category' or 'concatenate' - a false ENTAILED verdict, which is the exact failure mode the product exists to prevent. Guarded by a dedicated regression test.

nodes.label: Hybrid Search via Reciprocal Rank Fusion
nodes.norm_label: hybrid search via reciprocal rank fusion
nodes.rationale: Dense pgvector ANN and sparse Postgres full-text ranking are merged by RANK POSITION (score = sum of 1/(k+rank), k=60) rather than by blending raw, differently-scaled distance and rank values - the two scales are not comparable.

nodes.label: Pure-Function Query Builders
nodes.rationale: build_vector_search_query and build_keyword_search_query take no session and touch no DB, so Postgres-only SQL generation is unit-testable without a live Postgres instance.

nodes.label: Dependency-Override Testability Seam
nodes.rationale: get_hybrid_retriever exists purely as an override point: hybrid_search issues Postgres-only SQL (<=>, to_tsvector) SQLite cannot execute, so tests swap the retriever for a stub while chunk CONTENT is still read from a real in-memory DB via a portable WHERE id IN (...) - generation and verification stay exercised against genuine data.

nodes.label: EventSource Is GET-Only - Needs fetch + ReadableStream
nodes.norm_label: eventsource is get-only - needs fetch + readablestream
nodes.rationale: The query stream is a POST, and the native EventSource API only supports GET, so Module 7 needs a manual fetch + ReadableStream SSE frame parser. Recorded in the plan now rather than discovered during implementation.

nodes.label: SSE Event Contract (token/verification/done/error)
nodes.rationale: Four event types in a fixed order: tokens stream first, then per-claim verification rows, then a final done carrying overall_score and is_fully_supported. This is the contract the frontend audit-log pane is built against.

nodes.label: Explicit Extension Whitelist
nodes.rationale: SUPPORTED_SUFFIXES is an allow-list, not a deny-list, so an unknown or disguised extension (invoice.pdf.exe) fails closed with HTTP 400.
